**Route table**

| Route | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/ai/mentor/chat` (Ask Mobi) | capped: `buildReplyDeps` passes `...spendUserFor(user)` (id plus paid/free tier) | unchanged |
| `/api/recovery/repair` (Mistake Repair, explanation and blind check) | capped: `spendUser: spendUserFor`, `...route, ...spend` on both calls | unchanged |
| `/api/ai/rival/start` (intro) | not capped: no userId or tier | capped: `...spendUserFor(dbUser)` |
| `/api/ai/rival/submit` (outro) | not capped: no userId or tier | capped: `...spendUserFor(dbUser \|\| session.user)` |
| `/api/internal/moderation/process` | user-less by design; the route answers 503 and spends nothing | unchanged |
| Other `/api/ai/**` routes (actions/execute, context, credits and its order/verify, mentor history/local/report/session/new, usage) | never reach a model | unchanged |

The rival fix is the same patch as commit 2ee6deea on `web/fix-pricing-1017`. Identical hunks should merge cleanly. If the paid-plan lookup fails in the submit route, it falls back to the session user, which only ever gets the stricter free cap.

**Migration**
- `supabase/migrations/20261017120000_runtime_ai_user_cap.sql` now seeds the paid cap at 0.0568. It had 0.1136, so a fresh database would have come up at Rs 10.
- I added a note saying production already matches. The insert stays "on conflict do nothing", so a re-apply never overwrites a changed cap.
- Nothing needs applying to production.
- On a fresh database only, the global `student_ai` row would still seed USD 25 from `20261004120000_runtime_ai_monthly_cap.sql`. Production's row is 1000000. I left that file alone and noted it in the migration.

**Tests**
- New `data/tests/ai_cap_route_coverage.test.mjs`, added to `test:learning`. Its cases:
  - Every model caller in `src` is either declared student-capped or user-less.
  - Only `providers.js` creates provider clients.
  - The real `reserveRuntime` is exercised with PostgREST-shaped results and errors (jsonb as the data object, `P0001` errors mapped to user_budget, budget, model_not_allowed, guard_paused and price).
  - A call with no request key is refused before the database is asked.
  - The paid or free plan is read from the stored user.
  - The migration seed values are checked.
- `ai_user_cap.test.mjs` is updated to the Rs 5 numbers and has a rival-route test.

**Decision for the owner**
- Both rival routes pass no request key. `reserveRuntime` refuses any call without one, so the rival intro and outro have never reached a model since the guard was added. Students always get the fixed lines.
- That is why nothing was being overspent. It is also why passing the user id and tier is a safeguard for now, not a live cost change.
- I did not add request keys. Doing so would turn on real spend for decorative lines and use up the small Rs 1 free cap that Ask Mobi and Repair also draw from.

The `node_modules` junction was first created with a broken target. I recreated it and verified it resolves to the hotfix `node_modules`.
